Our GC flagged the limitation of liability section — specifically the interplay between the damage cap and the exceptions for fraud/willful misconduct and gross negligence. Looping you both in — BrightTail pushed an aggressive set of redlines on caps vs misconduct. Quick notes:
- They want fraud/willful misconduct to be an absolute carve-out (no cap). We typically accept carve-outs for proven fraud and criminal acts but prefer to gate on a high evidentiary standard and a materiality threshold so opportunistic claims don't blow past the cap.
- Ask from procurement: define evidentiary standard and whether 'reckless' sits inside or outside the cap.
- Timebox: they want a response by Thu EOD.

Can Legal propose a narrow definition and an evidence-gating process we can propose back — e.g., requirement to provide an evidence matrix + independent investigator or arbitration step before cap is removed? Also confirm what we can accept for indemnity triggers.

Thanks — Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: MSA draft — carve-outs for fraud/willful misconduct

Karthik / Jordan —

Draft proposal below for response to BrightTail. I kept the language surgical to reduce surprise:

1) "Carve-out for Fraud/Willful Misconduct": Proven intentional fraud or criminal act (as reflected in a final judgment or a binding arbitration award) shall not be subject to the aggregate liability cap. Claims that are based on reckless or negligent conduct remain subject to the cap.

2) "Evidentiary gating": Prior to treating a claim as a carve-out, the claimant must submit a written evidence matrix detailing specific allegations and supporting documentation. If the parties do not agree on the sufficiency of the evidence, the parties will jointly appoint an independent third-party investigator (or proceed to expedited arbitration) to determine whether the misconduct meets the carve-out standard. The costs of the investigator or arbitration shall be borne by the prevailing party.

3) "Materiality threshold": The carve-out applies only where the misconduct resulted in material harm (defined as direct damages exceeding USD 250,000 or demonstrable regulatory penalty).

4) "Indemnity and criminal fraud": Redwood will accept that criminal fraud (conviction or binding criminal restitution order) will be excluded from the cap. For civil fraud claims, the carve-out applies only if the evidentiary gating concludes fraud by clear and convincing evidence.

Notes: the materiality dollar threshold is negotiable depending on deal economics. Also propose adding an explicit survival period for evidence (e.g., retain materials for 2 years) if BrightTail insists on audit rights.

Attached is a one-page evidence_matrix_template.xlsx we can share to operationalize. If you both sign off, I will turn this into redline language and send to BrightTail.

—Lauren
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Keegan <skeegan@brighttail.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: BrightTail Contracts <contracts@brighttail.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: MSA draft — carve-outs for fraud/willful misconduct

Lauren — thanks for the detailed proposal. A few immediate reactions from our side: 1) BrightTail is concerned that an investigator/arbitrator step adds delay and complexity before victims can seek recovery; we propose an expedited neutral review with a 21-day clock and shared costs upfront. 2) The USD 250k materiality is high for SMB data exposures — can we instead tie materiality to either (a) a regulatory penalty or (b) demonstrable customer impact (notice to >1,000 users or system unavailability >8 hours)? 3) Clear and convincing is acceptable for civil fraud carve-outs; we would prefer no cap for 'reckless' if reckless involves deliberate circumvention of controls.

We can be flexible on process if you accept a slightly broader carve-out on recklessness.

Looking forward to your redline language.

—Sara
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: MSA draft — carve-outs for fraud/willful misconduct

Quick commercial read: BrightTail is a growth account (expected 18 month ARR $1.2M). We should be careful about an unconditional reckless carve-out — that's a meaningful exposure. Suggest two levers for negotiation:

- Move the materiality threshold down from $250k to $50k but add a two-tier remedy (statutory damages / separate bucket for customer remediation not counting toward aggregate cap).
- Agree to a 21-day expedited review process (neutral reviewer) but require BrightTail to post a security hold and provide the evidence matrix up front; if reviewer finds for claimant, costs are split 50/50.

If Legal can produce redline language reflecting that, I will take to procurement and tell them we are willing to compromise.

—Jordan
VP, Sales Operations
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Keegan <skeegan@brighttail.com>, BrightTail Contracts <contracts@brighttail.com>

Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA draft — carve-outs for fraud/willful misconduct

Sara — attaching proposed redline language (see attached PDF) that implements Lauren's evidence gating with two commercial tweaks Jordan recommended: lower materiality to USD 50,000 with a separate remediation bucket and a 21-day expedited neutral review. Key points:

- Criminal fraud remains an absolute carve-out (no cap), supported by conviction or binding order.
- Civil fraud requires clear and convincing evidence through the evidence matrix and neutral review.
- Reckless conduct that involves deliberate circumvention of contractual security controls and results in material harm as defined will be eligible for carve-out; ordinary negligence does not qualify.
- Costs for the neutral review are split 50/50; prevailing party may recover costs.

Please confirm if this is acceptable or propose final tweak by EOD Fri so we can finish SOW/order form.

Best — Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
